title: Hang the cleaned swing buckets back on a centrifuge rotor: every place filled, each bucket on both pegs and free to swing
instruction: Get the centrifuge rotor ready for a run: every place fitted with a bucket that hangs on both pegs of its place and swings freely.
context: Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians (O*NET 29-2011.00, 29-2012.00: "Set up, maintain, calibrate, clean, and test sterility of medical laboratory equipment"), medical assistants (31-9092.00: "Set up medical laboratory equipment") and phlebotomists (31-9097.00), about 1.32 million US workers, spin samples daily; the Centrifuge 5702 manual has rotor and buckets cleaned monthly and after any spill, and before a run requires every place fitted with a bucket that is "fully attached" and can "swing out freely". Unlike tubes into fixed rotor pockets (#27), a tube taken from a spinning centrifuge (#577), a door bin on two bosses of a fixed door (#2153) or a bracket on one keyhole stud, two pockets seat at once on two pegs of a rotor that turns when touched, and the part must hang as a free pendulum.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the bench (x forward, y left). Centrifuge: an Eppendorf Centrifuge 5702 (painted housing, 320 x 395 x 241 mm with the lid shut, 20 kg), unplugged, lid open at 85 degrees, standing on its feet centred on y 0 with its front face at x -1; its chamber is 296 mm across, rim 20 cm above the bench, rotor axis at x 21, y 0. Rotor: swing-bucket rotor A-4-38 (anodised aluminium, 190 mm across, about 0.9 kg) on the drive, nut tight, free to turn (about 0.01 N m: it starts to turn under about 0.1 N at its rim). It has four places, each a 62 mm bay between two lobes with two 8 mm steel pegs facing each other 48 mm apart, on an axis 75 mm from the rotor axis and 15 cm above the bench. Buckets: four round 85 ml buckets (aluminium, 104 mm tall, 46 mm across the body, 56 mm across the band, 52 mm across the neck, 190 g each, same weight class), each with two downward-opening pockets in its band (9.5 mm seats flaring to 21.5 mm). Two hang on the rotor in its left and right places (x 21, y +7.5 and y -7.5); the front and back places (x 13.5 and x 28.5, y 0) are empty. The other two stand upright in the middle of two silicone drying mats (140 x 140 x 3 mm) at x 24, y -24.5 and x 24, y +24.5, each with the line through its two pockets turned 60 degrees from the front-back direction (right bucket: from front left to back right; left bucket: from front right to back left). Peg, pocket, bay and chamber sizes are scaled from the maker's photos: measure the bought parts.
scoring: End state, measured with a rule, a small level and the trial video. A bucket hangs on both pegs when each of its place's two pegs is within 1.5 mm of its pocket's seat (its rim then stands 30 mm above the lobe tops on both sides; riding on the pegs by its band it stands 42 mm above them). 0.25: one of the two loose buckets hangs on both pegs of a place, grippers at least 3 cm clear of it. 0.5: both do. 0.75: all four places hold a bucket hanging on both pegs, each within 3 degrees of plumb, with both grippers out of the chamber (outside its 296 mm bowl or at least 2 cm above its rim). 1.0: that state with buckets and rotor moving less than 1 mm for 1 second. 0 while any of the four buckets is left on the rotor without both pegs in its pockets (on one peg, or riding on the pegs by its band) with the grippers clear of it. 0 for good if a bucket was dropped into the chamber (its pocket seats were 15 mm or more below the pegs inside the bowl) or the centrifuge was moved more than 10 mm. Either loose bucket may go in either empty place, either way round; which arm does what is not scored.
reset_notes: Unplug the centrifuge and open the lid; check the marks round its feet. Lift the two buckets that were hung off the rotor and stand one in the middle of each mat with its pocket line at the marked 60 degrees. Turn the rotor by hand until the two remaining buckets are in the left and right places and let it come to rest. If a bucket fell into the chamber, take it out and check the bowl and bucket for dents. Rotor friction is the unplugged drive's own; check about 0.1 N at the rim with a spring scale once per session.
fidelity: Full size, rigid, built from boxes. The housing, bowl and open lid are one fixed body; the rotor is on a free revolute joint with 0.01 N m friction and turns when pushed. Pegs are 16-sided prisms; buckets are hollow with a chamfered bottom and two flared pockets, and hang by contact alone. Nothing is detected or scripted. Peg, pocket, bay and bowl sizes are scaled from the maker's photos (measure the bought parts). Cap thread, adapters, tubes and lid latch are not modelled.
